issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() should return a String, but the solution changes the abstract method signature to return a FeedResponse. This is a structural mismatch: students implementing messageOnFeed() to return String (as required by the assignment) will find the solution uses a different return type and an extra FeedResponse class, which may cause confusion about the intended API and return value semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent: either revert the solution to match the specification by having Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and have Pig/Seal/Goat return String), or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly specify that messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse and document the FeedResponse class and its semantics. Preferably, align the solution with the original UML (return String) to avoid introducing an undocumented type in the reference solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning a String (messageOnFeed():String) and the task text describes feed messages as String values (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). The solution changes the return type to a custom class FeedResponse (Animal.messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse and a FeedResponse class is introduced). This introduces a new identifier (FeedResponse) not present in the problem statement or template and changes the expected method signature, which can confuse students about the required return type and how to implement/print feed messages.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type of messageOnFeed() across problem, template, and solution. Either: (A) Change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and remove FeedResponse), returning the feed message strings directly (matching the UML and task text), or (B) Update the problem statement and template to specify and document the FeedResponse type (its fields and intended use) and require messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. Option A is simpler and keeps the API consistent with the exercise description.
